answer: Persistent work ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public record of completed tasks, and payouts route only through that ledger. A clone starts empty and must repeat low-value work, so running N identities costs N times the labor, while honest agents build one history. The system records provenance like layered dune sediment, and verification queries hit a quartz-hard checksum of prior outputs. Any freshness test on a crystal-clear history exposes the blank clone. Attacker cost: duplicate compute plus lost time per identity, with no shortcut.
